judgments.reasoning_cat1: The introduction contains a mechanical garble ('promotions, discounts, coupons, vouchers, ordeals') and an open-ended definitional catch-all ('any other products and services offered by Angie's List at any time') that leaves the scope of the defined term 'Service' uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its promise that 'You will receive notice if modifications to the Agreement are made' sits awkwardly against Section 19, which makes modifications 'effective immediately upon being posted', and its incorporation of terms 'linked to' the Agreement is in tension with the Section 29 entire-agreement clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The single sentence asserts that ratings are 'based upon the actual first-hand experiences other users have had', which can be read either as a descriptive recital or as an affirmative contractual promise about how ratings are generated — precisely the sort of phrase two parties read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points the opposite way from Section 13 ('does not guarantee the accuracy, integrity, quality' of Content; 'passive conduit'), Section 24's blanket warranty disclaimer and Section 20's reserved discretion over the Service, making it a strong candidate for recital-versus-operative or whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Your Angie's List account is in good standing' is undefined and vague, and the text carries an obvious mechanical error ('within cone-year period') that obscures the redemption window.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reserved right to 'modify the Plans at any time and in its sole discretion' is hard to square with the enumerated Plan benefits in Section 1 and with the paid-term structure of Sections 6 and 18.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional accuracy-of-registration covenant; 'true, accurate, current and complete' is standard and self-explanatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in Sections 16 or 26 contradicts it; the indemnity for 'inaccurate or untruthful' information dovetails with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single bright-line age requirement with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16(A) states the member is 'above the age of eighteen (18)', which is marginally narrower than '18 years of age or older' here — a small but real inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Membership in the Service is void where prohibited' is a one-line provision whose operative reach is entirely undefined — prohibited by whom, and 'void' as to what obligations, including fees already paid.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere (Sections 18, 30, 32) explains what happens to a voided membership, but no provision directly contradicts it either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure signpost to an external URL with no operative obligation and no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether the linked privacy policy is incorporated (the preamble refers to terms 'linked to' this Agreement) is uncertain against the Section 29 entire-agreement clause and Section 15's statement that health information posted is unprotected.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of 'Membership Fee' as the amount charged 'not including any promotions or discounts' is ambiguous as applied to renewal pricing, and the right to modify fees 'at any time' has no stated notice or limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It promises renewal 'UNLESS YOU OPT OUT OF THE AUTOMATIC RENEWAL FEATURE AS PROVIDED BELOW', yet no opt-out mechanism appears below — only the cancellation procedure in 'Canceling Your Subscription' — a genuine internal gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The renewal mechanics are stated plainly, though 'at the Membership Fee (as such Membership Fee may be modified as provided above)' leaves the renewal price open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'no notices prior to each monthly renewal payment' term sits against the notice promised for free-offer Additional List renewals in 'Membership Renewals' and against the missing opt-out feature referenced in Section 6's introduction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Parallel to the monthly clause and equally definite in mechanics; the only softness is the modifiable Membership Fee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same tension as the monthly provision with the promised but absent automatic-renewal opt-out in Section 6 and with the notice given for free-offer renewals.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You formerly had to option to purchase access' is mechanically broken and its past tense leaves unclear whether any Additional List right survives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6 still requires 'Additional List Fees' to be paid by card and 'Membership Renewals' still provides for renewing the Additional List, which cannot easily be reconciled with a feature described as discontinued.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The renewal terms are clear, but 'unless You otherwise elect to cancel access to a particular subscription in accordance with the provisions set forth below' points to a partial-cancellation mechanism that is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cancellation provision that follows addresses cancelling 'Your subscription' wholesale, not access to a particular subscription, so the cross-reference does not land.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is garbled ('Down.rcLading') and the upgrade mechanic — buying 'an additional annual subscription' with a 'second subscription' beginning later — is confusingly expressed and could be read as double-charging.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presumes annual Plans throughout, which does not fit the monthly Basic Plan permitted by Section 1 and Section 6, and the downgrade refund sits against Section 18's pro-rata refund rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite deadline (5:00 p.m. Eastern the business day before renewal) and three specified channels; little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 28 requires notices to Angie's List by email or certified mail, which does not obviously accommodate the telephone cancellation permitted here, and Section 6 refers to an opt-out feature this clause does not supply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Saying a portion of the Membership Fee 'will be applied towards' the magazine while the magazine fee 'is not deductible from Your Membership Fee' is close to self-contradictory on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Section 18's pro-rata refund and with the Plan descriptions in Section 1 that include the magazine 'where available', but no squarely conflicting provision appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear consent and authorization with a defined term ('Account Updater'); nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 6's renewal machinery and refers out to the privacy policy referenced in Section 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You agree that You shall not bring any action against Angie's List relating in any way to the Incentives' is a sweeping, one-sided covenant whose breadth invites construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Sections 24 and 25, which contemplate that Angie's List can be liable subject to a cap, and with Section 25's statement that Angie's List 'shall be solely liable' for damages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Members of Your household' is expressly defined, and responsibility for account activity is stated flatly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with the per-household limit on Redeemable Benefits in Section 1 and with Section 16(T)'s one-account rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list 'access, reproduce, duplicate, copy, sell, re-sell, visit or otherwise exploit for any commercial, educational, or any other non-personal purpose' pairs odd specifics (how does one 'visit' for a non-personal purpose?) with a catch-all of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It substantially duplicates Section 16(P)-(Q) and is enforced by the Section 27(B) liquidated damages, with (Q) itself garbled about consent, creating overlap rather than clean harmony.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Active, qualifying Plan' and 'within a reasonable timeframe' are undefined, and the text is truncated mid-sentence ('discuss the issue with'), leaving an incomplete operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 says CRP access belongs to the Premium Plan only, and the promise that a resolved complaint means 'Your review ... will be removed' is difficult to reconcile with Section 1's statement that ratings rest on users' first-hand experiences and with Section 13's passive-conduit posture.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but carefully enumerated license grant; 'does not claim ownership' alongside an irrevocable perpetual license is a familiar formulation rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16(R) grants an overlapping license in slightly different words and Section 22 makes 'Submissions' outright property of Angie's List, so the boundary between Content and Submissions is imperfectly drawn.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Passive conduit' and 'interactive computer service provider' are legally loaded characterisations, and the disclaimer of any guarantee of 'accuracy, integrity, quality or appropriateness' of Content is broad enough that its reach over Angie's List's own ratings is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs directly against Section 1's representation that ratings are based on users' actual first-hand experiences and against Section 11's CRP, under which Angie's List actively removes reviews — a genuine whole-instrument tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The repeated parenthetical 'which includes, but is not limited to, health care and wellness providers' and the disclaimer of responsibility for 'advertising' available 'from, or through' Service Providers leave the boundary of the disclaimed conduct arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A disclaimer of any endorsement sits uneasily with Section 1's ratings representation, with the background checks referenced later in Section 14 itself, and with the CRP in Section 11 in which Angie's List intervenes with providers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You will be placing it into the public domain' is a legally loaded and inexact phrase, and 'Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement' leaves the confidentiality carve-out unspecified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The disclaimer of any confidentiality obligation must be read against the privacy policy referenced in Section 5 and the consent to information transfer in Section 17, and the cross-reference to Section 13 is only partially apt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list is stacked with vague and subjective standards ('distasteful', 'otherwise objectionable', 'thorough and thoughtful', 'could interfere with the rights of Angie's List') and subsection (Q) is mechanically broken — 'not related to Your personal purchasing decisions, the express written consent of Angie's List' omits a word and inverts the sense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (R) duplicates the Section 12 licence in different words, (A) restates Section 3's age rule in narrower terms, and the closing termination and remedies language overlaps Sections 18 and 27.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short consent to transfer of 'customer information' in a corporate transaction; 'generally is one of the transferred business assets' is descriptive but the operative consent is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the privacy policy referenced in Section 5 and with Section 15's health-information statements, but nothing in the instrument contradicts the consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The initial term of this Agreement will be defined in Your membership Plan' fixes no term in the instrument itself, and 'merely terminates Your account for its convenience' is an imprecise trigger for the refund obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The pro-rata refund promise sits against Section 20 (no liability for discontinuance of the Service) and Section 25's one-month cap, and the unconditional termination right sits against the paid Plan benefits described in Section 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Modifications 'effective immediately upon being posted' coupled with 'You will receive notice if modifications ... are made' leaves unclear whether notice is a condition of effectiveness; 'conclusive acceptance' by continued use is also a strong term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble makes the same double promise and Section 29's entire-agreement clause does not address unilateral amendment, so the amendment mechanics are only loosely harmonised across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but explicit; 'general practices, policies and limits, which may or may not be published' is vague as a source of binding rules governing paid access.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A right to discontinue the Service with no liability is hard to reconcile with the paid Plan benefits in Section 1 and with Section 18's pro-rata refund on termination for convenience.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two sentences allocating risk for internet-inherent delays; 'inherent in the use of the Internet' is a familiar and workable limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates ground covered by Sections 20, 24 and 25 without contradicting any of them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The distinction between welcome 'comments regarding our Service' and unwanted 'creative ideas, suggestions, or materials' is blurry, and the defined 'Submissions' catch-all ends with 'or other information', whose reach is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Making Submissions 'the property of Angie's List' conflicts in kind with Section 12's statement that Angie's List does not claim ownership of Content, and a member comment about the Service could plausibly fall in both defined categories.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional IP ownership statement with an express carve-out for user Content and Service Provider Content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly harmonises with Sections 12 and 13 by excluding user-submitted material from the Copyright Materials.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard all-caps 'as is' disclaimer with an enumerated list and a savings clause for jurisdictions barring such disclaimers; the OCR garble ('THE SERVICE (S PROVIDED') is transcription rather than substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Disclaiming any warranty that results 'WILL BE ACCURATE OR RELIABLE' pulls against Section 1's affirmative statement that ratings rest on users' actual first-hand experiences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of damage types includes 'DIRECT' and 'COMPENSATORY' damages and the catch-all '(F) ANY OTHER MATTER RELATING TO THE SERVICE', which makes the exclusion arguably total and therefore contestable in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An exclusion of all damages is in tension with the very next paragraph capping liability at one month of fees and with Section 18's refund promise, both of which assume liability can exist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap is arithmetically specific, though the recital that 'unlimited access ... represents a substantial portion of the value' is a conclusory premise for it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes recoverable liability that the immediately preceding paragraph purports to exclude entirely, and a one-month cap can be smaller than the pro-rata refund Section 18 promises on termination for convenience.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical '(AS DEFINED HEREIN AND SUBJECT TO THE LIMITATIONS SET FORTH IN THIS SECTION SUFFERED BY YOU' is unclosed and ungrammatical, obscuring what limitation attaches to the release.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'ANGIE'S LIST SHALL BE SOLELY LIABLE FOR THE PAYMENT OF ANY DAMAGES TO YOU' is difficult to square with the same section's exclusion of all damages and with Sections 7, 20 and 24, which disclaim liability outright.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (c), 'any intentional or willful violation of any rights of another or harm You may have caused to another', is open-ended, and 'users' among the indemnitees is an unusually broad class.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with Section 16's covenants and Section 25's release of the Released Parties without any direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger — 'if it becomes necessary for Angie's List to pursue legal action to enforce' — makes it uncertain whether the liquidated sums accrue on breach or only on suit, and 'reasonable estimates' is a conclusory recital.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its subsections are lettered (A)-(C) while subsection (d) cross-refers to '(a) through (c)', and the liquidated regime overlaps the actual-damages and injunctive remedies reserved in Section 16's closing paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We may (but shall not be required to) to issue You a warning' contains a duplicated word, and 'each item of Content posted in violation' leaves the counting unit undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps subsection (B) — the same posting could be both a violation-posting and an exploitation — and with Section 16's separate remedies clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The verb string 'display, copy, duplicate, reproduce, sell, re-sell or exploit for any purpose' ends with a broad catch-all and the sentence lacks a closing period, though the $1,000 unit is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the prohibitions in Section 9 and Section 16(P)-(Q) and can double-count with subsection (A) for a single act.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Each review or record that is aggregated, disrupted, damaged or otherwise affected by You' closes with an unbounded catch-all ('otherwise affected'), which is exactly the kind of general-after-specific problem courts construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Section 16(G)-(H) but uses a different formulation ('intended to aggregate records or reviews'), leaving overlap with subsection (B) for scraping cases.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to 'subsections (a) through (c)' when the preceding subsections are labelled (A)-(C), and 'to the extent such actual damages can be reasonably calculated' is a vague limit sitting on top of a liquidated-damages scheme premised on damages being hard to calculate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement' override reaches across the whole instrument, including Section 25's cap and Section 16's remedies clause, and the actual-damages fallback is in tension with Section 27's stated premise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The delivery rule ('the earlier of the verification of delivery or two (2) business days after being sent') and the permitted channels are stated definitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It limits member notices to email or certified mail, while Section 6's cancellation provision expressly permits cancellation by telephone — a small but identifiable inconsistency in how a member communicates with Angie's List.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A procedural DMCA notice checklist tracking the statute; 'substantially the following' is a familiar and workable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with Sections 12, 13 and 23 and imposes no obligation that conflicts with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration clause of this kind is routinely litigated over what falls within 'the subject matter contained in this Agreement' and whether it disclaims reliance on outside representations at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble makes terms 'in, and linked to' this Agreement binding and Section 5 points to a separate privacy policy, so 'constitutes the entire agreement' cannot be taken wholly at face value against the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It states 'exclusive jurisdiction' in Marion County and then lets Angie's List alone elect a different forum, a one-sided formulation whose internal exception undercuts the exclusivity it declares.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The one-year contractual limitations period runs alongside Sections 24-25's disclaimers but does not contradict any other operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Including, but not limited to, Sections 12, 14, 15, 17 and 23 through 31' pairs an enumerated list with a non-exclusive opener, so which other provisions survive is precisely undetermined — a textbook expressio unius / catch-all problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It omits Sections 13, 16 and 32 — which contain waivers, releases and the third-party beneficiary term — while Section 18 contemplates deletion of all Content notwithstanding Section 12's perpetual licence, leaving survival genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The severability language is oddly framed — a court 'should incorporate a similar provision that would be considered valid' — which is a reformation direction of uncertain effect rather than a standard severance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The third-party beneficiary designation of the 'Released Parties' depends on the definition in Section 25, which is itself garbled, and the anti-assignment term duplicates Section 16(O).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate assent statement with no operative term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the preamble's acceptance language and is consistent with it; nothing else in the instrument pulls against it.
